# Strygonia

> Strygonia builds precision bench instruments for embedded engineers.

## About

Strygonia is a hardware company that designs tools for engineers who work with embedded systems, PCBs, and microcontrollers. Founded by Sidak Mann.

Website: https://www.strygonia.com
Contact: contact@strygonia.com
YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@Strygonia
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/Strygonia/

## BlackBox (SG-BB1)

A hardware flight recorder for your bench.

- Type: Hardware flight recorder
- Price: $198.99 (Founder's Edition, first production run)
- Status: V1 prototype
- Buy: https://www.strygonia.com/reserve
- Product page: https://www.strygonia.com/products/blackbox

### Summary

BlackBox is a small module you clip onto almost any embedded system (a breadboard, a Raspberry Pi, a custom PCB) and leave running. It keeps a rolling record of the signals you check first when something goes wrong. So instead of trying to make a crash happen again, you just scrub back through the timeline and watch it play out.

### Features

- Watches power-rail voltage on up to two rails and flags brownouts and startup dips
- Tracks board current the whole time, and marks the spikes and odd draws when they happen
- Captures every line of UART: boot logs, debug prints, each one timestamped
- Catches resets as they land, whether it's the watchdog, a brownout, or your finger on the button
- Four GPIO inputs you can name, plus one analog channel for whatever else you're watching
- One color-coded harness for breadboards, Pi headers, and test points; one USB-C cable to the app

### How it works

BlackBox runs continuously while your board runs, keeping a rolling window of every channel. The failure is already recorded by the time you notice it.

1. Your board: Whatever you're already working on: breadboard, Raspberry Pi, or a custom PCB.
2. The harness: One color-coded bundle clips onto power, ground, UART, reset, and the pins you pick.
3. BlackBox: Sits beside the board and samples every channel against one shared clock.
4. Rolling buffer: Onboard memory keeps the most recent window, overwriting the oldest as it goes.
5. USB-C: A single cable carries both power and the recording back to your machine.
6. The timeline: Desktop app you scrub through. Graphs, event markers, and the serial log lined up.

### V1 channels

Six inputs on one harness. Every sample shares the same clock, so a voltage dip, current spike, and the serial print that preceded them line up on one timeline.

- Power rails: Up to 2 rails, with brownout and startup-dip detection. Every change is timestamped, so you can see exactly when the voltage left its healthy band.
- Current: Board current the whole time, from a high-side sensor that flags spikes and unusual draws as they happen. The tell for a short or a stalled motor.
- UART: Full serial capture. Boot logs and firmware debug output, timestamped against the same clock as the analog channels so the print lines up with the fault.
- Reset line: Watchdog, brownout, and manual resets, caught the moment they land. So you know whether the board fell over or was pushed.
- GPIO x4: Four configurable inputs you name yourself. Motor Enable, Fault Pin, chip select, whatever you happen to be chasing this week.
- Analog in: One spare configurable channel for a battery rail, a thermistor, or any sensor output you want on the same timeline.

### Specifications

| Spec | Value |
|------|-------|
| Processor | 32-bit ARM microcontroller |
| Current sensor | High-side, precision |
| Storage | Onboard, rolling buffer |
| Link | USB-C to USB-C, power + data |
| Targets | Breadboard / Raspberry Pi / custom PCB |
| Status | V1 prototype |

Specs are subject to change as the hardware is validated. Full spec page: https://www.strygonia.com/specs

### What ships with it

- BlackBox V1 recorder in a printed enclosure
- Color-coded wiring harness with labelled leads
- USB-C cable for power and data
- Desktop timeline app for macOS, Windows, and Linux

### Compatible with

STM32, ESP32, Raspberry Pi, Arduino, KiCad projects, custom PCBs, breadboards, Rigol scopes, Saleae.
